Retroactive fix, discovered while building biology-12-3's stage 9 page. Root cause: the shared latex_convert.py's plain-prose escape path (_escape_prose, used for ALL text outside a $...$ math span) was unconditionally calling the same operator-padding function used for actual math content (_finish_plain_text), which wraps a bare '/' in non-breaking spaces on both sides - correct for a real division inside math, wrong for everyday English punctuation like 'True/False' or 'asexually/sexually', which this chapter's question text uses (a math-free Biology chapter routes 100% of its text through the prose path, so every bare '/' in it was affected). This visibly inserted a space into 4 items' own immutable question text on the already-shipped page: q_2.1(a)/(c)/(d)/(e)'s fill-in-the-blank prompts ('asexually / sexually', 'external / internal', 'diploid / haploid' x2) and all 7 of q_2.16's True/False sub-prompts ('True / False' -> should read 'True/False'). Fixed by splitting _finish_plain_text into two functions: _normalize_whitespace (newline/space collapsing only, now used by _escape_prose for plain prose) and _finish_plain_text (unchanged, still does the operator padding, now called only from inside the actual math-conversion buffer flush, where a bare '/' genuinely is a division). Rebuilt final.en.html with the fixed converter; re-ran the full stage-9 checklist (image resolution - 8/8 still resolve, numeric read-back - 1/1 still found, HTML artifact scan - 0 hits) with 0 new regressions. Also confirmed biology-12-1 has no bare-slash-in-prose content, so its own already-shipped page was never affected by this bug despite sharing the same converter.
